notes.title: New ores, gemstones, and other resources
notes.notes:
To help with the understanding of the crafting recipes, we modified the natural resources of the Aevian System.

On Merx, the "common" metal is now called [b]Ferroxyde[/b]. Solid, but easily transformed in a forge, it will be useful to make the first tools and weapons. Besides, Ferroxide ore can be found on the surface, in the scattered boulders in the plains. If an object needs to resist to high temperature, it will be better to design it using some [b]Calorium[/b], that can be found below the surface, in the yellow sandstone. Finally, in the chalky rocks, you will find some [b]Electrum[/b], that is mostly used in electric items.

Different gemstones also illuminate Merx caves: [b]Laserite[/b] (red) is used to create laser ammo and any other laser-involved objects. [b]Crystaline[/b] (white) is a hard gemstone used to cut and crush, in the gauntlet recipe, for example, and [b]Explodine[/b] (orange) will be used in different explosive recipes.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/8887a97e2bcf183204a8eb080d7cf9be12d22559.jpg[/img]

Istara also contains some useful metals: The [b]Steeltanium[/b] is harder than the Ferroxyde, and will allow you to build more resistant objects whereas the [b]Carboflex[/b], that is light and flexible, is a great natural and recyclable alternative to plastics since the last drops of petroleum have been used a few centuries ago, in the Aevian System. Istara's gemstones are the [b]Concentrite[/b] (yellow) that improves the properties of whatever it is mixed up with, the [b]Reversine[/b] (purple) that reverses some effects, and the [b]Silicine[/b] (blue), a semiconductor material that is used in most electronic circuits.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/454c46dda1cd8610fb23a7d32de76664edb5b7e7.jpg[/img]

Of course, lots of other resources are used in the crafting system: Plants, like [b]Mandragoras[/b], [b]Cotton[/b] or [b]Fire flowers[/b], [b]Mushrooms[/b], [b]Fur[/b], or even [b]Goo[/b], a slimy and sticky material created by spiders to protect their eggs...

notes.title: No more memory lapse!

For now, we introduce a single block. But we already know that this simple block will give headaches to the more adventurous of you. So, watch carefully the video below:

https://youtu.be/v3Dm4y2TbxY

As in the previous presentation, please look carefully at the bottom right tooltip, which allows us to know the value carried by a cable.

Here is a simple example: the memory allows keeping the door open after we walked in front of the sensor. But just imagine the possibilities allowed by that such a block!

In the next and final part of this presentation, we will make together a step more toward automation of complex systems.

notes.title: 256 values!
notes.notes:
Welcome to the second presentation about the new logic system. Here we will see that the cables do not simply carry a binary value, meaning 0 or 1. In fact, the logical cables carry values between 0 and 255. The video below shows some applications of this property:

https://youtu.be/XZPff2P0sgI

When you change the value of a potentiometer or activate an infrared detector, it changes the value transmitted by the cables. Look carefully at the values displayed in the bottom right tooltip, which allows us to know the value carried by a cable.

At the end of the video, we see all the logic gates that allow to manipulate these values. They are divided into two categories.

Logic gates of the first category are put on the top line in the video. They return either 0 or 255, but not an intermediate value.

Logic gates of the second category are put on the bottom line. They return a number between 0 and 255.

It begins to become interesting, isn’t it? Wait to see the next episode!

notes.title: After Beat EP2: Music on Merx
notes.notes:
Hi everybody! Last time, we saw how I used a leitmotiv to characterize our character's journey, today I will tell you a little more about the music of Merx.

[b]The leitmotiv of Merx:[/b]

Again? Yes, indeed, I used a leitmotiv also for the planets sometimes. But here it is even more simple and basic than for our character, it is not really a melody, but just [b]3 successive notes[/b], making it much more malleable, adaptable to the various situations encountered on the planet.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/f00f2ac6f8723a3f04b98cb62edd9211945c0452.png[/img]

This small figure can be heard for the first time in the village [b](at 0.15 precisely)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZK4UqnVqPQ&feature=youtu.be&t=15s

Then we will hear it everywhere on the planet, for example here at Li King Pei’s house, very quickly [b]at the beginning of the theme[/b], and then played by a Japanese flute [b](at 0.29)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kDwBp3N6SEc&feature=youtu.be&t=29s

Merx is the starting planet. With Reymantha, we call it [b]la-la land[/b]. Everything is beautiful, calm, and very (nearly too much) naive. I obviously wanted people to feel it, almost humorously, with very soft, relaxing, and cute music at the same time. That’s why it’s mostly played by a flute, or a piccolo, the most aerial and light instruments, as here in the grasslands of Merx [b](at 0.34 precisely)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D4lwbLNlZac&feature=youtu.be&t=34s

A small anecdote, this theme, by its lightness, its naiveté, and its aerial side supposed to represent the song of the birds, is a small reference to a studio Ghibli film that I like very much: [b]The Tale of the Princess Kaguya[/b], more precisely the theme representing the joie de vivre of the main character at the beginning of the film [b](from the beginning of the music)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZNfbVEXItRk&feature=youtu.be

By creating this small 3-notes pattern, which will be modified in a large number of musics, I thus introduce [b]a musical peculiarity to Merx[/b], which, if it can’t be felt from the beginning (because there are no points of comparison in the adventure), will take its full meaning medium-term and long-term, without (at least I hope) becoming a too annoying melody.

[b]Instrumentation:[/b]

This notion of leitmotiv is not only felt in this small figure but also in [b]the instruments chosen to represent this planet[/b]. I choose a set of precise instruments for each planet, and even if I authorize myself a few exceptions, I try to remain faithful to this, for more coherence.

The basic instruments I chose for Merx are: flute, piccolo, folk guitar, harp, violins, soft synths. An example with a good part of these instruments in this excerpt [b](starting from 4.20)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=D4lwbLNlZac&feature=youtu.be&t=4m20s

Flutes, harps, or violins are often used in video games, the folk guitar is much less. It's a touch that I liked, because with percussion and synths, it allowed me to have a slightly [b]"weird bossa nova" style[/b]. Here I am inspired by the soft guitar musics of Ian Snyder in [b]The Floor is Jelly[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DWt-t0YwXmY&feature=youtu.be

But the whole principle of what I try to do on the planets is in the [b]hourly evolution of the music[/b]. The basic idea, as most often, comes from a problem related to gameplay: the planets are cubic, so one can almost instantaneously go from day to night. This is the basis of my reflection: how can we go from day to night, or from morning to dusk, without shocking the ear? Elements of response are in [b]the video that follows[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QpSTxgIgmuY

What is heard in this video is that [b]the orchestration and even the melodies evolve over time[/b], becoming more and more electronic and abstract when the night comes, and conversely more and more organic and real by day. The process consists in the creation of several musics, of strictly equal lengths, and similar harmonies.

The hourly cycle of the game will then pass these musics from one state to another, in a fluid way, and it will function if the player stays on the same side of the planet or if he decides to change abruptly. In the next example, I will [b]make the music pass from day to night and then to dusk[/b], which is normally totally illogical, but entirely possible with the structure of our game:

https://soundcloud.com/cubicaldrift/day-to-night-to-dusk

It is almost the same principle that is applied to the environmental sounds, and that is more easily understood via the sound interface that we use in our game (Wwise):

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/44ccaab8844c74988b1f52345a0c7d0926f9deea.png[/img]

Here we see that following the advance of the time of day, different [b]atmospheres can blend into each other[/b]. 

There you have the basic things I used to create the music of Merx. There are still a lot of things to talk about, especially in caves or underwater, but I cannot explain everything. In the next episode, we will concentrate on [b]the small details, anecdotes, allusions or references[/b], hidden here and there in the music of Stellar Overload.

I hope you enjoyed this episode, see you soon!

notes.title: After Beat EP1: Leitmotiv
notes.notes:
Hi everybody, I am super happy to present you today the first After Beat article, in which I will dissect the music of the game.

Let’s start with a question that almost nobody asks itself except me: [b]is there a leitmotiv in the game?[/b]

Well, since not everyone is necessarily a specialist in music, we will first define what a leitmotiv is. Let’s take the Oxford dictionary definition, which is very clear: 
[b][i]«Leitmotiv: A recurrent theme throughout a musical or literary composition, associated with a particular person, idea, or situation».[/i][/b]

So, did I use a leitmotiv in Stellar Overload? Yes, and even several, for factions, characters, etc. But today we will just focus on the most important: [b]the leitmotiv of our character. [/b]

It consists of a short melody of 8 notes (just because 8 is my favorite number, that's it...) that we will be able to hear for the first time in the main menu of the game, towards the very end [b](At 03.42 precisely)[/b]. Concentrate on your left ear and spot it played by a kind of "electronic flute":

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yaM8klGIK88&feature=youtu.be&t=3m41s

This little melodic figure, which stumbles but always arrives higher, is there to represent the difficult task of our hero. All this is also perceived visually by taking a glance at the score and the way it is composed:

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/af76a76dc68f67853dcf673a4d542b085b14a533.png[/img]

Following the curve drawn by the course of the notes, one sees well the stumbling side but which always goes up higher.

And I hid this leitmotiv in many important places of the adventure, either related to the scenario, or related to particular gameplay situations. For example, here in the cinematic intro of the game, played at the Glockenspiel, the first time we see our character asleep [b](at 0.30 precisely)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S6badE21opk&feature=youtu.be&t=28s

The rebels are an important part of the formation of our character, thus the music of their camp on Merx also contains this theme sometimes [b](at 0.16 for example[/b], in a little more serious tone than before):

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tVt1FcxRj_c&feature=youtu.be&t=15s

It is also present but modified in victorious jingles, or even in the captured music of an enemy building, where the victory of our character mingles with that of the rebels [b](at 0.15 precisely)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BoQdKpLGkNA&feature=youtu.be&t=15s

The last example, more subtle and emotional, when we find our brother in the lab, here with the figure engrained on the piano to bring back a little tenderness in a place yet conducive to combat [b](from 0.37)[/b]:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a3ZUyUkX1qQ&feature=youtu.be&t=36s

Let’s finish with [b]a really hidden detail[/b]. If several jingles obviously use the leitmotiv, it is much more hidden in the « medium » jingle, when you get a recipe kind of reward. In the excerpt that follows, you can hear the jingle [b]at its normal speed then slowed down strongly[/b], clearly revealing the melody:

https://soundcloud.com/cubicaldrift/jingle-medium

There are other examples of the presence of this melody in other musics of the game, or even in some trailers, but I let you find them by yourself now. I hope you enjoyed this little article, next time we will talk about [b]the music of Merx[/b]!

See you soon, Keep on rocking!

notes.title: Early Access Update 3, let's go!
notes.notes:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Xvo0zOnCEE
 
We are more than happy to present the new update (0.8.7.0) of Stellar Overload!
Find below the list of the main new features available in this update.
 

[b]Electricity[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/2bd701fb6a930499ddc433425c69d84797e8cdfa.jpg[/img]
A brand-new feature has been added to the game: [b]electricity[/b]!
In this very first version, you can have fun with switches, cables, batteries, doors, lasers, NOT gates and AND gates.  

To be more specific, we chose to separate [b]logic[/b] and [b]power supply[/b]. You have to handle both systems at the same time:

- Be sure supply power to your items with batteries and powercables (otherwise they may not function that well)

- Control your items with switches through logical cables
 
[i]You can have more information in game pressing F1 (or TAB), we added a specific part in the codex for the electricity.[/i]
 

[b]Motorail[/b]
 
https://youtu.be/JIKK1zXwygA

A new type of vehicle is coming: a motor on a rail. We decided to call it "Motorail"!
To function, it has to be connected to a battery and to at least one switch…
 
[b]Those two elements (motorail and electricity) can seem pretty trivial but it actually multiply the creative potential of the game.[/b]
We cannot wait to see what you’ll do with it!
 

[b]The HookBlade[/b]
 
https://youtu.be/3qiOOtc-WN0

It’s been a while since you have been asking us to add melee weapons. There you are: there is a blade in the game!
At the same time, we added a functionality to it: the grapple. The grapple allows the player to have more mobility.
You will find the Hookblade in the inventory in the creative mode (use the new “weapon” filter).
In story mode, you’ll find it during your adventure.
 
[i]For now, the grapple only functions on walls. But we are planning on improving its uses and making it possible to target enemies.[/i]
 

[b]Novo Ares[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/82b6cd5e513e449759671fef7dd9b95d9bd3ea12.jpg[/img]
 
An update = a new planet. This time, we progressed pretty well on the Novo Ares planet.
Novo Ares is a very specific planet: very arid in the surface and tropical at the bottom of its canyons.
 
 
[b]Syntonized Stellarium Lab[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/9241b3fc826b38adfb9852ce2204f278f10677c7.jpg[/img]

Here is the true dungeon of Merx : the [b]Syntonized Stellarium Lab[/b].
 
Robots took over an ancient human lab where humans did some research on Stellarium. Stellarium is a material about which we do not know much. We have to take back this lab!
 
[i]Do not look for the old fortress, we erased it from the game.[/i]
 
 
[b]Other interesting functions[/b]
 
- Share [b]universes on Steam Workshop[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/a9f6abaecd27d4ce66daa5471a9e962304a02d8d.jpg[/img]

Did you create a big dungeon? [b]You can now share it worldwide![/b]
[i]Everything happens on the universe loading screen.[/i]

- [b]Hunger[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/165dbb6efbb634518da5effe2252e16771e82688.jpg[/img]

You asked for it, it finally is in game. Some items now restore hunger, others restore life.

- [b]Difficulty levels[/b]

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/a6443e0ace7696f1b9bd4caba8b24952e02ae2bb.jpg[/img]

When creating a game (or loading it), you can now configure several difficulty options (such as make enemies easier to kill, activate hunger…)

- [b]Block physics[/b]

It is still at an experimental level so it is not activated by default. However, you can test it by activating it in the game creation window.
 
 
All that is only a part of the main new features of this version. You can find all the latest novelties in details in the updated release note [url=http://www.stellar-overload.com/the-game/release-notes.html?rn=21 target=blank]here[/url].
 
[i][b]Note for all AZERTY players[/b]: you have to reconfigure your keyboard.  You will find a new button, in the top right-hand corner of the option window to settle all the shortcuts into AZERTY. [/i]
 
As usual, do not hesitate to tell us what you think on our forum or on social networks. We gladly read all of your remarks.
 
But above all: [b]have fun![/b]

notes.title: Steam Early Access Update 2 : it's today!
notes.notes:
We are glad to present the 0.8.6.0 early access update! 
Here are the main new features you will find: 

[h1]Istara[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/f07400afcc8c2ac592ceac5fccfc2f48724fecd9.jpg[/img]

Our second planet, Istara, has been highly improved, graphically and technically. 
Istara is a cold forest planet with three biomes in it: the swamps, the sequoïa forest and snowy forest. 
A new population of animals appeared : spiders, brakhs (a local boar) and bees. 
New trees were also added: pines, spruces and above all, the giants sequoïas.  


[h1]New vehicle : the Spacejet[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/daa7846ca86f18750d1aa7cc58b38488ef8e4510.jpg[/img]

3 new control blocks have been added: the Gyrograv block, the Spacejet cockpit and a directionnal thruster. 
You can now get into space by building a spacejet with those new elements! 

The thrusters allow you to control the direction of your ship. You will need 6 thrusters, one for each direction to fully control your ship (Forward, backward, move laterally to the left, or to the right, up and down). 
If you put only 2 blocks forward and backward for instance, you will just be able to go forward or backward. 

Do not forget to check the key bindings options: we added a vehicle section so you can set your bindings according to your preferences, with no effect to the character bindings (on foot). 


[h1]Workshop on Steam feature : Share your plans with the community![/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/31155649c3b2864c383293b610e79c4d9aa8c484.jpg[/img]

You want to show to the community your brand new spaceship you just made? You want to try a house a friend of yours did?
By pressing the “P” key while in game, you will open the plan sharing tool. 
This tool allow you to share every plans you created with all your local saves, but also with the rest of the world directly on Steam Workshop. 
Just drag and drop a plan from this new screen to your inventory and put it in your world (if you have the right blocks to build it!) 
Just drag and drop a plan from your inventory to the workshop, add it and bam! It’s online!


[h1]New community feature: Transforming a creative universe into a custom universe[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/8f4526b0813fcaa28659efe213d72c4c1fa149f7.jpg[/img]

Build your world in creative mode, then transform it into a custom universe (“C” button on the universe’s list). The custom mode is your universe with no scenario. You will start with an empty inventory and a knowledge of every recipes. 
More options to customise this mode will be added in the future. 


[h1]New features for the creative mode[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/e2cece8258e80af2d8bda3b8fb7a6eb7309f7abd.jpg[/img]

You can now put creatures to create your own swarming dungeon! Eww... !

You can now define the spawn point for the players by using the /setspawn command. Use it for example to set the spawn point in front of your dungeon.

You can also enable or disable the inertia using the command /togglemomentum. Our artist team asked for this option, and some of you will definitely like it too!


[h1]Recorder improvement, and plan setting enhancement[/h1] 

Right click now registers automatically an object. The algorithm now spreads to all the blocks linked to the one you are targeting. You’d better separate your object from the ground before you do that ;)


[h1]New death system[/h1]

Death is always hard to balance and above all, today we don’t have every tool to do it. 
From now on, when you die, you will loose all your inventory but your weapons, ammo and armor.
You will need to come back where you died and click on the bag to loot your inventory. 
Make some backup chests before you go kill some monsters, who knows ;)


[h1]New quest log[/h1]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/26551395/f8ab073a129eab546b407a2bc22010f966cbb91e.jpg[/img]

You can now follow a secondary quest by selecting it from the journal (press “J” key) and by clicking on the “Follow” button on the top right corner.
3 characters will wave at you at a moment during the adventure (at the end). 
Keep an eye open ;)


You can also check every modifications and improvements we have done in the last seven weeks on the detailed release note of this new update [url=https://www.stellar-overload.com/the-game/release-notes.html]here[/url].

[h1]We hope you will enjoy these new features as much as we enjoyed making them![/h1]

[i][b]Note for all the AZERTY players[/b]: You need to reset your key bindings manually in the game options, due to the new spacejets mechanics, we currently can’t mix US and FR key settings anymore. We will provide a fix in a future patch regarding this issue.[/i]

[i][b]Note for the builders[/b]: you can now access the old “EA1” version to create all the  blueprints you want, and then copy them to the new version folder. To access the old version: right-click on Stellar Overload in your game list, choose “properties”, and go to the “betas” tab. Select the “steam_ea1_v0.8.5.2” version in the dropdown list.[/i]

As usual, we have open a new section on the forum. Do not hesitate to tell us your feelings about this new version of the game. 

And most importantly : [b]Have fun[/b]!
